record.paper_title: Enabling and Emerging Technologies for Social Distancing: A Comprehensive Survey and Open Problems
record.context_brief: AI cough detection at sensor range limits
record.original_question: How can acoustic-sensor and artificial-intelligence systems detect and localize coughing people in public places for social distancing when the sound source is far from the sensors and localization or measurement errors become large?

evidence.quote: In the social distancing context, this system can be applied directly to monitor and detect coughing people in public places. Nevertheless, a limitation of this system is that the localization and measurement errors increase significantly when the sound source is too far from the sensors.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a network of $N$ acoustic sensors deployed at known positions $\mathbf{s}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{s}_N \in \mathbb{R}^3$ in a public space, each producing a noisy time-domain signal $x_i(t) = a_i(\mathbf{p})\, c(t-\tau_i(\mathbf{p})) + n_i(t)$, where $c(t)$ is an unknown cough waveform from a source at unknown position $\mathbf{p}$, $\tau_i(\mathbf{p}) = \|\mathbf{p}-\mathbf{s}_i\|/v$ is the propagation delay at sound speed $v$, $a_i(\mathbf{p}) \propto 1/\|\mathbf{p}-\mathbf{s}_i\|$ is a distance-dependent attenuation, and $n_i(t)$ is ambient noise plus interference from non-cough sources. The detection problem requires deciding, from $\{x_i(t)\}_{i=1}^N$, whether a cough event occurred (a binary classification against speech, laughter, sneeze, traffic, etc.), and if so, estimating $\mathbf{p}$. Standard time-difference-of-arrival or beamforming localization combined with a learned cough classifier $f_\theta$ achieves bounded mean-squared localization error only when the source-to-array distance $d(\mathbf{p}) := \min_i \|\mathbf{p}-\mathbf{s}_i\|$ is small relative to the array aperture and signal-to-noise ratio is high; as $d(\mathbf{p})$ grows, both the classifier's accuracy and the localization variance degrade sharply.

Design a joint detection-and-localization algorithm — combining acoustic sensor processing with a learning-based component — that reliably detects and localizes coughing individuals in such an environment under the regime in which $d(\mathbf{p})$ is large and TDOA/energy-based measurement errors are no longer small perturbations. Specifically, give an algorithmic scheme together with conditions on the array geometry, sample complexity, signal model, and training data under which the probability of correct cough detection and the localization error remain controlled (e.g., bounded with high probability) as $d(\mathbf{p})$ approaches the practical sensing range limit.
artifact.status_search_result: No definitive solution to far-field cough detection-and-localization with bounded error has been published; existing AI-based cough detection systems (e.g., CNN/transformer audio classifiers and microphone-array TDOA methods) continue to report rapid degradation of accuracy and localization variance as source-sensor distance grows, and the problem is generally treated as open in the acoustic sensing literature.

status_evidence.title: Enabling and Emerging Technologies for Social Distancing (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Listed as an open problem: localization and measurement errors increase significantly when the sound source is too far from the sensors.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is identified as open in the surveying literature on social-distancing technologies.
